gemini.intro: To translate, I get a little help from Gemini, which is free. You just need your own key (it costs nothing and takes about as long as brewing a cup of tea):

gemini.privacidad: The key is stored encrypted on this PC and is never shown again. The text you translate is sent to Google; on the free plan, Google may use it to improve its products. Anything already translated is saved in your library and isn’t requested again.

configuracion.enAmazonTexto: In your Amazon account: Manage Your Content and Devices → Preferences → Personal Document Settings → add your Gmail address to the approved email list.
configuracion.importarDetalle: From the Kindle button in the top bar, or by dragging My Clippings.txt onto the window.
configuracion.familiaCompartida: This is a shared library (read-only): you can’t share from here. Open your own library to use Family.
configuracion.ultimaVersion: ✓ You’re up to date: you have the latest version ({version}).

configuracion.herramientasNota: Broots reads your library directly, but only changes it with these tools, one change at a time and with a backup first in .broots/respaldos.
configuracion.actualizacionNota: Broots checks on its own once a week. The download comes from the official Calibre site and is verified before it’s used.
configuracion.buscarVersion: Look for a new version of Calibre
configuracion.mismaVersion: Broots always uses the same version as your Calibre. To update it, open Calibre and look for the new version there (or download it from calibre-ebook.com).

traduccion.detalle: The text of the paragraphs you translate in the reader. Only if you added your key and turned translation on.

datos.dondeConAmazon: Amazon, Google Books and Open Library

drive.detalle: Your library and the Family copies are in Drive folders: they are uploaded by the Google Drive program on your PC, not by Broots.

calibre.detalle: If Calibre isn’t installed, Broots downloads its official copy and checks once a week for a new version. Nothing of yours is sent.

actualizaciones.detalle: Every time you open Broots (and every six hours if it stays open) it checks for a new version and, if there is one, downloads it. Nothing of yours is sent. You can turn it off in Settings → Updates.
actualizaciones.detalleApagado: Off: only when you click “Check now” in Updates. Nothing of yours is sent.

configuracion.privacidadNota: Broots has no servers of its own and no interest in snooping: your library, your highlights and your notes are never sent anywhere on their own.
configuracion.privacidadIntro: Broots works on your PC. This is the only thing that leaves it, and only when you use that feature:
configuracion.queSale: WHAT LEAVES AND WHERE IT GOES
configuracion.amazonNota: Off by default: Broots looks for details and covers on Google Books and Open Library, with the Calibre tool. When it’s on, it searches Amazon first, which usually has better covers. Pasting the address of a book’s page (from Amazon or any other site) always works.
configuracion.amazonInterruptor: Look for details and covers on Amazon
configuracion.clavesTexto: You type the Gmail app password and the Gemini key yourself; they are stored encrypted by Windows on this PC and Broots never shows them again.
configuracion.version: Version {version} · your pocket library, and Calibre’s good friend
configuracion.libreDetalle: GPL license version 3 (or later): you can use it, share it and change it. If you publish a changed version, it also has to be free and open source.
configuracion.creditosNota: Calibre is free software under the GPL license version 3.
configuracion.calibreDetalle: Broots stands on the shoulders of a giant: Calibre, by Kovid Goyal and its community. It uses Calibre’s tools to read formats and change your library.
configuracion.sonidoDetalle: “Party horn 2” by Joseph Sardin on BigSoundBank.com, royalty-free. Thanks for the noise.
configuracion.donacionesNota: Broots is free. If it brightens up your reading, you can lend a hand to the people who make it possible.
configuracion.donacionesPaises: Cafecito is for paying from Argentina; GitHub Sponsors, from any country.
configuracion.sponsors: Support the author on GitHub Sponsors

If there is, it downloads it quietly, checks that it arrived intact and installs it when you close Broots. When this is off, it only checks when you click “Check now”.

Just in case, Broots doesn’t erase them: it renames the .broots/habito folder to habito-borrado-… (with today’s date), where they can be recovered.

New version ready. Steadier than your plan to finish that 900-page classic you’ve been “about to start” since last year.
New version out. So addictive you’ll be up until 3 a.m. reading the release notes.

instalada: Update complete. Perfect for speed readers, PDF hoarders and organization nerds.

cafe: Installed successfully. No developers were harmed, but quite a few coffee beans gave their lives for the cause. Want to restock? The button’s right there.

If this version saved you a chapter’s worth of time, buy the person who makes it a coffee. Their nervous system will thank you.

estados.crearTitulo: Keep track of where each book stands
estados.crearTexto: Your library has no status column. Broots can create one in Calibre, using Calibre’s official tool, with these options: To read, Reading, Paused, Read and Abandoned. It backs up the database first. Calibre will see the column too.
estados.confirmar:
Broots will add a "Status" column to your Calibre library, using Calibre’s official tool, after backing up the database (in .broots/respaldos).

If Calibre is open, close it first.

Create it?
estados.pausaPorQue: The Calibre tools Broots uses can create columns, but can’t add options to an existing one. You can do it in Calibre in thirty seconds, just once:
estados.paso1: In Calibre, open Preferences → Add your own columns.
estados.paso2: Pick "{columna}" and click the pencil (Edit column).
estados.paso3: Under "Values", add ", {valor}" at the end, then click OK and Apply.
estados.paso4: Calibre asks to restart: let it, then come back here.

explica.libre: No clock in sight. Broots still notes how much you read, but never rushes you.

explica.capitulo: When the chapter ends, I’ll ask if you want to stop there (or squeeze in one more, obviously).
